transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-16
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marco Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Malhotra (NovaGrid - Procurement), Ethan Cole (NovaGrid - Security), Marta Ruiz (NovaGrid - Legal)
Shared links: short deck: https://redwood.example/novagrid-intro, security pack: https://redwood.example/security/dpa (shared live)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Purpose: vendor-gate onboarding and privileged-keys/KMS path check for marketplace integration.
- Main asks from NovaGrid: explicit KMS flow, RBAC for privileged keying, SLA for dedicated vs hosted, pricing for committed volume and egress/cost for private deployments.
- Agreed pilot runway + next steps captured at end.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Lena with Redwood, AE on this account, and Marco is our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya: Hi Lena, good thanks, busy week here but we have bandwidth for this. I'm Priya, head of procurement at NovaGrid.
[00:12] Ethan: Ethan here, security eng, hello.
[00:14] Marta: Marta, counsel, hello.
[00:18] Marco: Hi all, Marco, hi. I'll mostly drive the technical bits.
[00:21] Lena: Great — agenda: confirm procurement gate criteria, run through MSA/DPA exceptions, talk about priv-keying/KMS integration options (VPC on-prem, Redwood Dedicated, hosted), and pricing/committed usage. Leave time for legal Qs at the end. Sound good?
[00:30] Priya: Yes, sounds good.

[02:05] Marco: Ok jumping in — quick high level: Redwood provides three main deployments: hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC or on-prem). For NovaGrid's vendor gate questions, the important bits are where keys live and auditability. For privileged keying we have two common patterns: customer-managed KMS in a VPC with our private control plane, or Redwood-managed keys with HSM/KMS integration, depending on the customer's tolerance for key custody.
[02:35] Ethan: Quick clarifying q: when you say "customer-managed KMS in VPC" — does that mean we can keep keys in our AWS KMS and Redwood never has plaintext access?
[02:44] Marco: Yes that's the pattern. In VPC Private mode, the inference nodes are in your VPC and KMS calls happen inside your account. Redwood's control plane can be configured to never persist plaintext or cache long-term; we can do envelope encryption so keys never leave NovaGrid's KMS. There are a few implementation details — latency for E2E key unwrap, and local KV-cache behavior to consider.
[03:08] Ethan: Ok, good. Also audit logs — we need proof of key use and per-request traceability. What's your log retention?
[03:16] Marco: We emit audit events for each request, and in Private mode those logs can be exported to your cloud storage. For hosted mode we retain logs per the DPA, typical retention 90 days but we can discuss longer retention for enterprise SKUs.
[03:29] Marta: Is there scope in the MSA for explicit obligations around key custody and indemnities? In our experience we need vendor obligations spelled out — e.g. non‑access to plaintext, breach notification windows.
[03:41] Lena: Totally. We'll share an MSA redline summary. There are standard clauses we can accept; anything beyond that would be an exception. We'll put together a redline that highlights the key custody language.

[05:00] Priya: On procurement criteria, the gate is: SOC 2 type II, SSO (SAML) integration, KMS pattern, SLA for 99.9% latency for bounded inference tasks, and pricing committed tiers. Pricing is the one people fight over.
[05:18] Lena: Understood. For SOC 2 we have a pack and cert — we'll share SOC artifacts. SSO yes, SAML works with our console and RBAC. On SLA, we have different targets for hosted vs Dedicated; Dedicated has latency/throughput guarantees with an SLA and credits. Hosted is best‑effort baseline with best‑in‑class perf but no reserved capacity guarantee.
[05:39] Priya: So we would need Dedicated for production customer-facing workflows?
[05:44] Marco: If you need guaranteed p99 latency and committed capacity, Dedicated is the usual recommendation. One nuance: you can do a hybrid — Dedicated for high-SLA routes, hosted for backfill. Routing policy allows per-route model pinning and fallback to cheaper variants.

[07:12] Ethan: On the pricing mechanics for Dedicated — are we doing reserved GPUs, or a commit-per-month token model? How do you charge for KMS egress or inter-region traffic?
[07:24] Lena: For Dedicated it's typically a reserved capacity (monthly commit) plus usage for compute beyond the reserved baseline. For token charges we can map to per-token or per-embedding unit depending on the model. Egress/egress-like network costs are handled separately — if you're in our hosted region some traffic is absorbed, but for Private/VPC there's normal network billing and any cross-region transfer costs. We'll send a sample pricing spreadsheet.
[07:49] Priya: We need a clear example that shows a 3‑month pilot to production ramp with committed and uncommitted tiers so finance can model it.
[07:58] Lena: We'll include a few ramp scenarios.

[09:20] Marco: Technical note: when using customer KMS, model KV cache behavior matters. We sometimes maintain a short-lived cache to improve latency; that cache does not contain plaintext model weights or key material, but careful design is needed for prompt prefix caching so you don't force re-unwrapping per token.
[09:40] Ethan: That's maybe a stumbling block for us — we have a hard rule to limit any externally cached secret data. Can you provide a design doc?
[09:47] Marco: Yep, I'll attach our KMS+KV-cache whitepaper. Expect some text artifacts — we sometimes call it "KV cache" or spelled as "K-V cache" in different docs.

[11:05] Marta: Legal — what about data residency? Our customers in EU require data not leave the EU. Can the Private deploy be run in eu-west-1 and ensure logs and keys remain in-region?
[11:18] Marco: Yes, for Private (VPC) we can deploy in your region and ensure logs, metrics, and KMS interactions stay in‑region. We can also do an on‑prem package for air‑gapped setups but that adds ops time.
[11:30] Priya: Ops time = procurement calendar impact. If on‑prem, what's typical lead time?
[11:34] Marco: For on‑prem it's usually 8–12 weeks for deployment, validation, and SOC checklist. VPC Private is faster — often 2–4 weeks depending on network approvals.

[13:02] Priya: Can you confirm the security pack link again? We want the DPA, encryption spec, and SOC report.
[13:09] Lena: Yes — shared in the chat: https://redwood.example/security/dpa and I'll also email a single bundle with the redlines after this call.

[15:00] Ethan: Speaking of DPA — we have a standard set of security addendums. What's your flexibility on data deletion windows? We want a 30‑day purge option for ephemeral data and a 7‑day revert window for troubleshooting.
[15:17] Marco: Hosted mode generally has configurable retention. For Private mode, since storage sits in your account, you control deletion, but our control plane may still have metadata traces unless excluded — that's something for the DPA. We'll flag retention fields in the redline.

[17:00] Marta: On indemnities — our legal team wants to limit vendor liability for data breach to direct damages and cap at X. Historically we push for more narrow responsibilities if keys are customer‑managed.
[17:12] Lena: Yes, we can annotate the MSA — when keys are customer-managed we typically accept narrower vendor obligations since you control keying. We'll note that as a talking point for the redline.

[19:05] Priya: Back to procurement gate — we also want pricing carveouts for academic usage and lower volume proof-of-value. Can you offer a short-term pilot discount?
[19:16] Lena: We can provide a pilot credit; usually 3–6 weeks with a capped usage. For Marketplace partners we sometimes give extended trials if there's commercial alignment.

[21:40] Marco: Quick demo snippet — if you look at the console route config, you can pin a route to a Dedicated model variant, set canary percentages, and configure fallback to cheaper models. API calls show the route id, model id, and a request id for tracing. That request id flows to logs exported to your S3/GCS.
[22:05] Ethan: Does the request id include user identifiers or PII?
[22:10] Marco: Request id is opaque; the payload and any PII are subject to your retention policies. In Private mode we recommend stripping PII before logging unless you want it for observability.

[24:00] Priya: Any talk about third-party vendor gating? We have a list and a matrix — where do you fall?
[24:07] Marta: Yeah, we evaluate data classification, crypto posture, entitlements, and contract redlines.
[24:12] Lena: We'll fill out your vendor matrix. If you can send the template we'll populate and return with evidence links.

[26:33] Ethan: One more technical: for the KMS flows, do you support external HSM providers (e.g., HashiCorp Vault with HSM or vendor-managed HSM)?
[26:41] Marco: We support standard KMS APIs. HashiCorp Vault is commonly used; integration often leverages Vault's transit engine. For HSM-backed keys we usually integrate via your cloud KMS or customer HSM endpoints. We'll need to scope any custom connector work.

[28:55] Priya: Timeline question — procurement wants a decision by 2025-10-03. Is that realistic to get MSA redlines back and a pilot running?
[29:05] Lena: Yes, if we get your vendor matrix and the KMS provider details by 2025-09-18, we can get the MSA/DPA summary and pilot provisioning out in time for an internal decision by 10/3.

[31:20] Marta: One administrative — CRM deal id, can you put this into our tracker? We need a commercial point of contact; also we may engage an external marketplace review board.
[31:30] Lena: Sure, I'll create a short summary with the deal tag and share.

[33:40] Marco: I'll outline two pilot options: (A) VPC Private pilot using NovaGrid KMS with short-lived cache and SAML SSO; (B) Dedicated Reserved pool for high‑SLA route with Redwood-managed key lifecycle and extended audit retention. Option A meets tighter key custody, option B is faster for performance guarantees.
[33:59] Ethan: Option A is preferred from security POV. Option B maybe for customer-facing low-latency flows but we'd have to get comfortable with key custody.

[35:10] Priya: Any blockers for finance to sign off? We need sample P&L impact and committed spend scenarios.
[35:18] Lena: We'll attach the spreadsheet with several ramp scenarios — pilot, 6‑month ramp, yearly committed discount pricing.

[37:45] Marta: A couple of small legal asks — 1) include a breach notification timeline (48–72 hours), 2) proof-of-compliance clause for SOC 2 attestations annually, 3) a clause for export controls in case of regulated content.
[38:00] Lena: We'll include those as standard asks in the redline pack and call out which are exceptions.

[39:30] Priya: Ok this has been helpful. Can we record the exact owners and due dates?
[39:35] Lena: Yes — I'll transcribe action items in the follow-up and cc everyone.

[41:05] Marco: I'll kick off the VPC pilot provisioning once we have Ethan's allowlist and KMS ARN. We'll set up a short-live instance for 2 weeks for testing.
[41:16] Ethan: I'll share those today.

[43:20] Lena: Recap: Redwood will share MSA redline summary, security pack SOC2/DPA, a pricing spreadsheet with committed tiers and pilot credits, and Marco will spin up a VPC pilot once Ethan sends KMS details. NovaGrid will send vendor matrix and confirm decision timeline (target 2025-10-03). Action items and owners recorded in chat.
[43:50] Priya: Thank you — we'll look for the docs and the matrix.
[43:55] Marta: Thanks everyone.
[44:00] Lena: Thanks all, we'll follow-up by email.
[44:05] Ethan: Appreciate it.
[44:10] Marco: Bye.

End of transcript.
